belongs_to: In-text question: "∆ABC is isosceles with AB = AC, and ∠A = 80. What can we say about ∠B and ∠C?" (followed by "Construct the altitude from A to BC.")
description: One isosceles triangle ABC, apex A at the top, B at the bottom-left, C at the bottom-right, BC horizontal at the bottom. The triangle is wider than tall (base about 1.7 times the height, so the apex angle is 80 degrees). Vertex labels: A above the apex, B to the left of the bottom-left corner, C to the right of the bottom-right corner. Marks: one short tick across AB and one short tick across AC (single-tick = AB equals AC); BC has no tick. A small arc is drawn inside the triangle at A, with the label 80° written just below the arc inside the triangle. No marks at B or C, no altitude drawn, no other points.

belongs_to: Proof that angles opposite equal sides are equal: "We have AB = AC (given), ∠ADB = ∠ADC = 90° (from construction), AD is a common side of the two triangles ∆ADB and ∆ADC" (the triangle of p.17 with the altitude from A constructed)
description: The same isosceles triangle as on p.17 (apex A at top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, base BC horizontal, same proportions: base about 1.7 times the height) with the altitude AD drawn. D is a point on BC exactly below A (the midpoint of BC) and is labelled D below the base. AD is a vertical line segment from A down to D. A small right-angle square is drawn at D, on the right side of AD, between DA and DC. Marks: one tick across AB and one tick across AC (single tick = equal); no tick on AD, BD, DC or BC. No 80° label and no angle arc at A in this picture. Labels: A above the apex, B left of bottom-left corner, C right of bottom-right corner, D below the base.

belongs_to: "What can we say about their angles?" - "The sides AB and AC are equal. So ∠B = ∠C."
description: One triangle ABC that is drawn equilateral (base BC horizontal; height about 0.87 of the base), apex A at the top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right. Marks: one tick across AB and one tick across AC (these two sides marked equal); BC has no tick. A single small arc is drawn inside the triangle at B and an identical single small arc at C (marking ∠B = ∠C); no arc at A. Labels: A above the apex, B left of bottom-left, C right of bottom-right. No numbers.

belongs_to: Second copy of the equilateral triangle, used for "Similarly, the sides AB and BC are equal. So ∠A = ∠C." (text continues on p.19)
description: One triangle ABC drawn equilateral, same size and position of vertices as P18-shape-2 (A apex at top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, BC horizontal). Marks: one tick across AB and one tick across BC (the tick on BC is vertical, at the middle of the base); AC has no tick. A single small arc inside the triangle at A (just below the apex) and an identical single small arc at C (marking ∠A = ∠C); no arc at B. Labels: A above the apex, B left of bottom-left, C right of bottom-right. No numbers.

belongs_to: "Congruent Triangles in Real Life ... Describe the congruent triangles you see in each picture." - caption "World-famous Louvre Museum in Paris"
description: Colour photograph (top-left of a 2 x 2 block of four pictures), caption in italics below: "World-famous Louvre Museum in Paris". Shows the glass pyramid of the Louvre at dusk/night, lit gold-yellow from inside, with its mirror image reflected in the water below it (the reflection fills the lower part of the photo). The pyramid face is a lattice of many small triangles (glass panes) formed by crossing diagonal bars. On the right is the lit stone Louvre building with a dark orange-brown sky. No numbers or labels.
unclear: Exact count of the glass-pane triangles cannot be read from the photograph; it is a photograph, not a drawn figure.

belongs_to: "Describe the congruent triangles you see in each picture." - caption "Rangoli design"
description: Coloured drawn rangoli design (bottom-right of the 2 x 2 block, a rectangle wider than tall, about 4:3), caption in italics below: "Rangoli design". Background: bright yellow. Thin olive-green lines run in two diagonal directions (down-right and up-right, crossing) and divide the whole rectangle into a lattice of yellow diamonds (rhombuses wider than tall). Centre: a four-armed pinwheel/star made of right-angled triangles, each coloured either dark blue or magenta-purple; blue and magenta triangles alternate round the star. Counted: 8 blue triangles and 8 magenta triangles in the central pinwheel; each of these triangles has one horizontal or one vertical side, and its other sides lie on the diagonal lattice lines. Corners: each of the four corners of the rectangle has two small magenta triangles meeting at the lattice line (8 corner triangles in all). No numbers or labels.
unclear: Exact count of the lattice diamonds and which individual triangle of the pinwheel is blue or magenta was not verified triangle by triangle; the 8 + 8 count of the pinwheel and 8 magenta corner triangles are from a close look and may be off by one or two.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q3: "It is given that OB = OC, and OA = OD. Show that AB is parallel to CD. [Hint: AD is a transversal for these two lines. Are there any equal alternate angles?]"
description: A bow-tie figure of two triangles meeting at O. Points: A at the top-left, C at the top-right (a little lower than A), O at the centre where two straight line segments cross, B at the bottom-left, D at the bottom-right (a little lower than B). Drawn segments (6 in all): AD (a straight line from A through O to D), BC (a straight line from B through O to C), plus AB and CD (the two outer sides, AB slanting from A down to B, CD slanting from C down to D). AB slants from A (top-left) down to B (bottom-left), CD slants from C (top-right) down to D (bottom-right); the two slants lean the same way, so the figure looks like a bow-tie with AB on the left and CD on the right. Marks: one tick across AO and one tick across OD (OA = OD, single tick); two ticks across OC and two ticks across BO (OB = OC, double tick). AB and CD carry no tick marks. No angle arcs, no numbers. Labels: A, C, O, B, D each beside its point (O just above the crossing).

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q4: "ABCD is a square. Show that ∆ABC ≅ ∆ADC. Is ∆ABC also congruent to ∆CDA?"
description: A square ABCD: A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, D at the bottom-left (in order round the square). The diagonal AC is drawn from the top-left corner A to the bottom-right corner C, splitting the square into the two triangles ABC (upper-right half) and ADC (lower-left half). No tick marks, no right-angle marks, no angle arcs and no numbers. Labels: A and B above the top corners, D and C below the bottom corners.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q5: "Find ∠B and ∠C, if A is the centre of the circle."
description: A circle with centre A (centre point labelled A, drawn just at the centre). Two points B and C lie on the circle, B at the left and C at the right, on a horizontal chord BC that lies below the centre (about halfway between the centre and the bottom of the circle, so the chord is at distance radius x cos 60° below A). Drawn: the chord BC (horizontal), and the two radii AB and AC, so ∆ABC is an isosceles triangle with apex A at the top. At A a small arc inside the triangle marks the angle BAC and the label 120° is written below the arc, inside the triangle. No tick marks and no other labels. Labels: A above the centre, B at the left of the left end of the chord, C at the right of the right end.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q6: "Find the missing angles. As per the convention that we have been following, all line segments marked with a single '|' are equal to each other and those marked with a double '|' are equal to each other, etc."
description: One large figure: a wide rectangle (width about 1.5 times the height) with 10 labelled points on its boundary and 4 unlabelled dots inside it, joined by many segments. RECTANGLE: corners C (top-left), D (top-right), A (bottom-left), B (bottom-right). Right-angle squares are drawn at C and at B. LABELLED POINTS ON THE SIDES (as fractions of the side from its first corner): R on the top side CD at 0.33 from C; V on the top side at 0.67 from C; so C-R-V-D are in this order with CR, RV, VD each marked with ONE tick. U on the left side CA at the midpoint (CU and UA each carry ONE tick). F on the right side DB at about 0.36 of the way down from D (F is above the middle of the right side). K and L on the bottom side AB at about 0.27 and 0.63 from A; K and L are in this order A-K-L-B. KL and LB each carry THREE ticks. FB carries TWO ticks (on the right side, between F and B). FOUR UNLABELLED INTERIOR DOTS (names below are only my own for this description, the book gives them no letters): P1 at about (0.33 across, 0.40 down), about 40 percent of the way down from R towards K; P2 at about (0.54 across, 0.45 down), the busiest point (seven segments meet there); P3 at about (0.31 across, 0.68 down); P4 at about (0.63 across, 0.68 down), directly above L. SEGMENTS DRAWN (besides the 4 rectangle sides): UR; UP1; UP3; RP1; P1P3; P3K (R-P1-P3-K runs from R near-vertically down to K, bending slightly at P1 and P3); RP2 continuing in the same straight line to P4 (R-P2-P4 straight); VP2; DP2; FP2; P1P2; AP3 continuing straight to P2 (A-P3-P2 straight); P3P4 horizontal; KP4 continuing straight to F (K-P4-F straight); P4B; P4L (vertical, ending at L). TICKS: ONE tick on each of CR, RV, VD, CU, UA, UP1, UP3, VP2 (8 single-tick segments). TWO ticks on each of P4F, P4B, FB. THREE ticks on each of RP2, AP3, KL, LB. ANGLE MARKS AND LABELS (arc + number unless noted): right-angle square at C (between CD and CA); 34° at R between RP1 and RP2; 68° at V between VR (the top side, to the left) and VP2; 98° at F between FD (up) and FP2; 34° at U between UP1 and UP3; 44° at P2 between P2R and P2P1; 46° at P2 between P2P1 and P2P3; right-angle square with the label 90° at P2 between P2P3 and P2P4; 56° at P4 between P4P2 and P4P3; 30° at P4 between P4P3 and P4K; 44° at P3 between P3A and P3K; 56° at A between AC (the left side, up) and AP3; 34° at A between AP3 and AB; right-angle square at L (between LP4 and LB); right-angle square at B (between BA and BD). Printed degree numbers in the whole figure (12): 34, 68, 98, 34, 44, 46, 90, 56, 30, 44, 56, 34. Right-angle squares (4): at C, at P2, at L, at B. Every dot (labelled and unlabelled) is drawn as a filled black dot. Point letters sit outside the rectangle for C, D, A, B, K, L, U, F and above the top side for R, V.
unclear: The four interior dots carry no letters in the book; P1-P4 are names invented for this description.
R-P1-P3-K are slightly bent, so whether the book means one straight line R-K with two points on it or three separate pieces cannot be told; P1, P3 are drawn as dots on it either way.
Positions are read off the page picture to about 1-2 percent of the figure size; angle values are exactly as printed.

belongs_to: Puzzle Time - "Expression Engineer!": "Draw lines and split the region consisting of white squares into 6 smaller congruent regions."
description: A square grid of 5 rows x 5 columns of equal squares (25 squares), drawn with thin grey lines and a grey outer border. 24 of the squares are white; exactly one square is coloured green with a thin red outline: the centre square (row 3, column 3). No numbers, letters, dots or other marks. The student has to cut the 24-square white region (a 5x5 square with the middle square removed) into 6 congruent pieces by drawing lines along the grid. (The pale-green page panel, the owl banner and the row of children below the grid are decoration and not part of the figure.)
